results.summary: This project is a simple 8-bit, single-cycle processor with a RISC-V-style instruction set and an accumulator-based data path. It has no internal instruction memory; the 16-bit instruction is applied externally through the 8 input pins and 8 bidirectional pins. Testing requires driving those pins with switches, an MCU, or an FPGA, and the design is intended for educational use or small embedded control logic. The documentation notes that manual switch input is impractical, so an external microcontroller such as an ESP32 is recommended.

This design implements Conway's Game of Life on a single Tiny Tapeout tile. It outputs a VGA video signal using the Tiny VGA pinout and runs at a 25.175 MHz clock. The project includes cocotb tests for verification and requires an external VGA screen to display the output. The documentation is very brief and does not describe the internal implementation or the initial pattern.

This project generates a VGA display that shows a checkers pattern based on a template from VGA playground. It was created during a workshop at Latchup and uses the Tiny VGA pinout. The design includes a test.py file for verification and requires an external VGA display to show the output. The documentation is minimal and does not specify the exact visual content or any unique features.

This project displays a moving screen strip on a VGA monitor using the Tiny VGA pinout. It runs at a 25.175 MHz clock and is tested with CocoTB. The design requires an external TV screen and an FPGA for operation. The documentation is very sparse and does not explain the visual effect or the internal logic.

This design is a 6-state finite state machine that manages power distribution across three prioritized loads based on undervoltage, medium-power, and high-power status flags. It includes a stability filter and staged load activation, with immediate de-escalation. Testing involves driving the flags and observing the enable outputs, and external hardware such as voltage comparators, MOSFET drivers, and LEDs is required to interface with real loads. The project is part of the IEEE Open-Silicon 2026 initiative and is implemented in pure digital logic without firmware.

This project implements a moving average digital low-pass filter, which is a type of FIR filter with equal coefficients. It processes a 12-bit input and produces a 12-bit filtered output, using the input pins and bidirectional pins for data. An external MCU or FPGA is needed to provide input data and collect the output, which can be observed with a logic analyzer. The design is part of the IEEE Open-Silicon initiative and is documented with its mathematical basis but lacks implementation details.

This project is an 8-bit quantized LSTM neural network accelerator for real-time wake word detection, specifically the word 'NYALA'. It accepts 7-bit signed audio features and a valid strobe, and outputs a trigger signal, confidence level, and busy flag. The design includes RTL and gate-level verification with cocotb, and it requires an external microphone and an RP2040 preprocessor for MFCC extraction. Notable features include a privacy-first smart home application and a fully digital inference pipeline.

This project reads eight digital input pins and transmits their states over a UART interface at 1,000,000 baud. It outputs a serial transmit line and a clock output. To use it, an external UART receiver must be connected to the transmit pin. The design is described as a 'useless logic analyzer' and has minimal documentation, but it functions as a simple pin-state monitor.

This project displays the Hackerspace Trójmiasto logo on a VGA monitor at 640x480 resolution. It includes a VGA timing generator and a bitmap ROM for the logo, with configurable color modes and animation such as bouncing or tiling. The design requires an external PMOD-to-VGA adapter to connect to a standard monitor. It is part of the IEEE Open-Silicon initiative and is fully synthesizable for ASIC implementation.

This project implements a finite state machine for a swarm microrobot drug delivery system, handling clot detection, communication, drug release, and motor control. It uses two inputs for local clot detection and nearby robot signals, and outputs drug release commands, transmission signals, and motor enables. The FSM has four states and includes a drug-available register that is cleared after release. No external hardware is required for the core logic, and the design is documented with a detailed test procedure.
